ROOT NEW EXACT CHECK ON THE FIXED FAMILY:
Let B^c_ij=P[F^c_ij.grad], B^s_ij=P[F^s_ij.grad]. On meanzero divergence-free trigonometricv,
 ||grad v||2^2 <= sum_(i!=j)(||B^c_ij v||2^2+||B^s_ij v||2^2) <=2||grad v||2^2.
Here is the usable calculation. Combining sine and cosine cancels cross terms between opposite frequency shifts:
 ||B^c_ij v||2^2+||B^s_ij v||2^2
 =2pi^2 sum_k k_i^2[||P_(k+e_j)v_k||^2+||P_(k-e_j)v_k||^2].
For integerk_i!=0 andj!=i, the angle betweenk andk+/-e_j hascosine>=1/sqrt2; thus each projection onk-perpendicular vectors preserves at least half squarednorm. Summing the two possiblej and threei gives the lower bound; contraction of each Leray projection gives the upper. Zeroshifts withk_i=0 contributezero. Consequently this family has NO common nonconstant kernel.

There is also NO nonzero COMMON INVARIANT SUBSPACE consisting of finitely supported Fourier fields. For a putative such finite-dimensional space, take its finite union of supports, choosei with somek_i=n!=0 and j!=i, then choose maximal k_j among that fixedn slice. The complex control B^c_ij+iB^s_ij=P[e^(2pi i x_j)partial_i] produces the UNIQUE nonzero coefficient at k+e_j, outside that union; the projection lower bound prevents cancellation. This proves precisely finite-FOURIER noninvariance, NOT absence of a general smooth/H1 finite-dimensional invariant subspace, a quantitative mixing rate or the full control theorem. These checks provide an actual opening; do not silently strengthen them.

## 1\. A new spectral reduction

The fixed-family problem has a useful route that requires **only three of the twelve permitted spatial fields**\:

\[
F_{12}^{c}=e_1\cos(2\pi x_2),\qquad
F_{23}^{c}=e_2\cos(2\pi x_3),\qquad
F_{31}^{c}=e_3\cos(2\pi x_1).
\]

The proposed mechanism is to use each field for one strong transport pulse, followed by a short diffusion interval. The three stages successively eliminate the components whose Fourier wavevectors have \(k_1\ne0\), \(k_2\ne0\), and \(k_3\ne0\)\.

The decisive advance is an exact reduction of each projected transport generator to one-dimensional Jacobi operators.

Fix \(i\ne j\), let \(\ell\) be the remaining coordinate, and write Fourier wavevectors as

\[
k=(n,m,l),\qquad n=k_i,\quad m=k_j,\quad l=k_\ell.
\]

On each fibre with \(n\ne0\), the operator

\[
B_{ij}=\mathbb P[\cos(2\pi x_j)\partial_i]
\]

preserves \(n,l\)\. After an orthogonal change of polarization basis, it becomes

\[
\boxed{
B_{ij}=i\pi n(J_0\oplus J_\rho),
}
\]

where \(J_0\) is the free bilateral Jacobi operator with off-diagonal coefficients one, while \(J_\rho\) has coefficients

\[
\rho_m=
\frac{r^2+m(m+1)}
{\sqrt{(r^2+m^2)(r^2+(m+1)^2)}},
\qquad r^2=n^2+l^2.
\]

An exact identity gives

\[
1-\rho_m=
\frac{r^2}
{\sqrt{(r^2+m^2)(r^2+(m+1)^2)}
\left[
\sqrt{(r^2+m^2)(r^2+(m+1)^2)}
+r^2+m(m+1)
\right]}.
\]

Consequently,

\[
0<\rho_m<1,\qquad
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}(1+|m|)|1-\rho_m|<\infty.
\]

Both Jacobi channels have no square-summable eigenvectors. For the weighted channel, the off-diagonal coefficients are a summable perturbation of the free recurrence; nontrivial solutions at interior spectral energies have nondecaying oscillatory asymptotics. The operator norm excludes exterior eigenvalues, and the strict coefficient inequality excludes eigenvalues at the spectral edges.
